promise_quote: Very ambitious next-generation experiments aim to be sensitive to conversion rates four orders of magnitude beyond the existing bounds, allowing them to reveal the presence of new particles with masses up to thousands of TeV, well beyond the reach of the LHC.
science_question: Detect muon-to-electron conversion in the presence of a nucleus as a signature of new physics.
rationale: Explicit recommendation to complete Mu2e; large project in Table 1; costs are only indicated by size class band (>$200M)

promise_quote: A new experiment, Muon g-2 at Fermilab, will significantly improve the accuracy of the measurement, and combining this with further improvements in the theoretical prediction for it may sharpen this discrepancy and point the way to new physics.
science_question: Measure the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon to unprecedented precision to search for deviations from Standard Model predictions.
rationale: Explicit recommendation to complete muon g-2; listed as large project in Table 1; costs indicated by size class band only

promise_quote: The HL-LHC has a compelling and comprehensive program that will make essential measurements of the Higgs properties.
science_question: Achieve percent-level precision studies of Higgs properties and search for new particles through high-luminosity LHC operations at 14 TeV.
rationale: Highest-priority near-term large project per Recommendation 10; large project in Table 1; U.S. participation in CERN facility

promise_quote: With these ingredients, combined with a baseline greater than 1000 km, LBNF can, with a single experiment, measure evidence for CP-violation in the lepton sector and provide a definite determination of the mass hierarchy, independent of the value of δCP.
science_question: Determine the neutrino mass hierarchy and measure CP violation in the lepton sector through long-baseline neutrino oscillation measurements.
rationale: Explicitly recommended as highest-priority large project in its timeframe; centerpiece of U.S. neutrino program; hosted at Fermilab; minimum requirements specified in text

promise_quote: The PIP-II project at Fermilab is a necessary investment in physics capability, enabling the world's most intense neutrino beam, providing the wideband capability for LBNF, as well as high proton intensities for other opportunities, and it is also an investment in national accelerator laboratory infrastructure.
science_question: Upgrade Fermilab accelerator complex to produce world's most intense neutrino beam (>1 MW) for LBNF.
rationale: Explicitly recommended; R&D to proceed immediately; necessary infrastructure for LBNF; provides >1 MW proton beam capability

promise_quote: The ILC would greatly increase the sensitivity to the Higgs boson interactions with the Standard Model particles, with particles in the dark sector, and with other new physics.
science_question: Measure Higgs boson properties to percent or sub-percent level precision using clean e+e- collisions at 500 GeV, upgradable to 1 TeV.
rationale: Japan-hosted international facility; U.S. engagement at appropriate levels; decision point within 5 years; physics case extremely strong; support across all scenarios

promise_quote: The Large Synoptic Survey Telescope (LSST) will precisely measure the positions and shapes of four billion galaxies along with estimates of their distances (using photometric redshifts), 100,000 massive galaxy clusters, and 250,000 Type Ia Supernovae, providing an order-of-magnitude improvement relative to current-generation experiments with structure measurements complementing the precise expansion history from DESI.
science_question: Survey four billion galaxies to measure cosmic structure and dark energy properties through gravitational lensing, galaxy cluster abundance, and supernova distances.
rationale: Explicitly recommended to complete as planned; medium project in Table 1; well underway; multi-agency success story

promise_quote: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) can provide very accurate distances to 25 million galaxies and quasars. The expansion history constraints from DESI BAO can be measured at the percent level, looking back over ten billion years.
science_question: Measure dark energy equation of state to percent precision by measuring expansion history through baryon acoustic oscillations in 25 million galaxies and quasars.
rationale: Conditionally recommended if funding permits; technically ready to proceed; interagency opportunity with Mayall facility; not possible in Scenario A

promise_quote: Proceed immediately with a broad second-generation (G2) dark matter direct detection program with capabilities described in the text. Invest in this program at a level significantly above that called for in the 2012 joint agency announcement of opportunity.
science_question: Detect dark matter particles through direct nuclear recoil measurements using multiple target materials and techniques across broad mass range (1 GeV to 100 TeV).
rationale: Explicit recommendation for broad G2 program; medium project in Table 1; should move forward immediately across all scenarios; increase investment above 2012 AO level

promise_quote: Support one or more third-generation (G3) direct detection experiments, guided by the results of the preceding searches. Seek a globally complementary program and increased international partnership in G3 experiments.
science_question: Measure dark matter particle properties comprehensively through next-generation ultra-sensitive direct detection experiments approaching neutrino background limits.
rationale: Explicit recommendation for G3 program; medium project in Table 1; reduced in Scenario A, full support in B and C; guided by G2 results

promise_quote: A Stage 4 Cosmic Microwave Background experiment (CMB-S4) aims at measuring the amplitude of the gravitational waves produced during inflation with percent level precision.
science_question: Measure primordial gravitational wave amplitude to percent precision to constrain ultra-high energy physics of inflation and test inflation models.
rationale: Supported as core particle physics program; multidisciplinary with continued multiagency partnerships; medium project in Table 1

promise_quote: The Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA) is the world's major step forward in ground-based gamma-ray astrophysics.
science_question: Search for dark matter annihilation signals in gamma rays through ground-based Cherenkov telescope observations of galactic center and dwarf galaxies.
rationale: Recommended conditionally as part of small projects portfolio if NSF Astronomy funding obtained; U.S. has distinctive technological contribution; dark matter detection capability

promise_quote: PINGU, an infill array concept at the IceCube facility, may also have the interesting potential to determine the neutrino mass hierarchy using atmospheric neutrinos sooner than other competing methods, as well as have sensitivity to low-mass WIMP dark matter.
science_question: Determine neutrino mass hierarchy using atmospheric neutrinos and search for low-mass WIMP dark matter through neutrino detection.
rationale: Further development encouraged; not yet ready for recommendation; could play important role as part of larger IceCube upgrade

promise_quote: Select and perform in the short term a set of small-scale short-baseline experiments that can conclusively address experimental hints of physics beyond the three-neutrino paradigm.
science_question: Test for sterile neutrinos and non-standard neutrino interactions through short-baseline oscillation measurements.
rationale: Explicit recommendation for portfolio of small-scale experiments; some should use liquid argon for LBNF technology development; addresses sterile neutrino hints

promise_quote: NuSTORM is a proposal for a small muon storage ring to produce ~GeV neutrinos and antineutrinos with the advantage of a precisely known flux.
science_question: Measure neutrino oscillation parameters and cross-sections with unprecedented precision using muon storage ring-produced neutrino beam.
rationale: Not recommended in any scenario; high cost makes it impossible to pursue simultaneously with PIP-II and LBNF

promise_quote: RADAR proposes to build a liquid argon TPC at the Ash River site, thereby offsetting R&D costs for LBNF.
science_question: Improve knowledge of neutrino oscillation parameters using liquid argon detector technology at NuMI beamline.
rationale: Not recommended; CP and mass hierarchy reach reduced compared to LBNF; less capable for proton decay and SN neutrinos; focus resources on LBNF instead

promise_quote: CHIPS proposes a large water Cherenkov detector in a water-filled mine pit, first at a NuMI off-axis location, and possibly later as an off-axis LBNF detector.
science_question: Improve neutrino oscillation measurements using water Cherenkov detector technology at NuMI beamline.
rationale: Not recommended; reduced CP and mass hierarchy reach compared to LBNF; strategy focuses resources on moving ahead as fast as possible on LBNF

promise_quote: The ORKA kaon experiment would provide an opportunity to make measurements of a process with very small theoretical uncertainties in the Standard Model with discovery potential for multi-TeV scale new physics.
science_question: Measure rare kaon decays with unprecedented precision to search for physics beyond the Standard Model.
rationale: Not recommended due to resource constraints and anticipated conflicts with Fermilab program priorities; complementary to CERN NA62 experiment

promise_quote: The Muon Accelerator Program (MAP) currently aims at technology feasibility studies for far-term muon storage rings for neutrino factories and for muon colliders, including the Muon Ionization Cooling Experiment (MICE) at the Rutherford Appleton Laboratory.
science_question: Develop muon ionization cooling and muon storage ring technology for future neutrino factories or muon colliders.
rationale: Reassessed per Recommendation 25; high θ13 value pushes neutrino factory timeline into far future; small Higgs mass favors e+e- colliders; MAP activities to be incorporated into general GARD program; MICE to be terminated in consultation with international partners

promise_quote: LAr1 is a mid-scale short-baseline accelerator-based experiment to address both the neutrino and antineutrino SBL anomalies.
science_question: Test short-baseline neutrino anomalies using liquid argon detector technology.
rationale: Not recommended; smaller combination of experiments can accomplish most goals at much lower cost
